## Xi Jinping in 2024: `1B.4` arms-control / disarmament / de-escalation in good faith

Best read: **Xi/China’s 2024 public posture was pro-arms-control in wording, but I did not find evidence of a new verified agreement, inspection regime, or disarmament step.** The clearest support is declaratory and policy-framing; the clearest counterweight is the continuing nuclear buildup, which makes the “good faith” claim less convincing.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports `1B.4` | [Nuclear arms control](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458633.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458633.html | China said nuclear arms control should reduce strategic risk, preserve stability, and proceed step by step. This is the most direct 2024 evidence of support for arms control/de-escalation language. | `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Supports `1B.4` | [No-first-use of Nuclear Weapons Initiative](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html | Official paper says Xi re-affirmed no first use and that nuclear war must not be fought. It also backs a mutual no-first-use treaty, which is a concrete arms-control preference. | `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.2` |
| Supports `1B.4` | [Security Assurances](https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng./xw/wjbxw/202407/t20240723_11458631.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng./xw/wjbxw/202407/t20240723_11458631.html | China called for unconditional negative security assurances, no first use, no threat of use against non-nuclear states, and reduced nuclear-alert practices. That is de-escalatory and consistent with arms-control good-faith signaling. | `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.2` |
| Supports `1B.4` | [Maintaining Global Strategic Stability, Reducing Risks of Nuclear Conflicts](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/gjhdq_665435/3376_665447/3432_664920/3435_664926/202406/t20240612_11428155.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-12 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/gjhdq_665435/3376_665447/3432_664920/3435_664926/202406/t20240612_11428155.html | China urged nuclear-weapon states to reduce the role of nuclear weapons, avoid launch-on-warning or pre-emptive doctrines, and avoid actions that spur arms races. This supports a de-escalation posture, though it is not a treaty commitment. | `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Weakens `1B.4` | [Role of nuclear weapons grows as geopolitical relations deteriorate - new SIPRI Yearbook out now](https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now) | SIPRI | 2024-06-17 | https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now | SIPRI reported China’s arsenal rising from 410 to 500 warheads and warned some warheads may be on missiles in peacetime. That does not disprove arms-control rhetoric, but it weakens a good-faith/disarmament interpretation. | `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Weakens `1B.4` | [Senior Defense Official Briefs on 2024 China Military Power Report](https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/) | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-12-18 | https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/ | DoD said China surpassed 600 operational nuclear warheads by mid-2024 and continued a rapid buildup. That is the strongest counterweight to a “good faith disarmament” reading. | `1B.4`, `1B.1` |

### Synthesis

- **Best support:** China publicly endorsed no-first-use, negative security assurances, and “step-by-step” arms control.
- **Best counterevidence:** China kept expanding its arsenal during the same period.
- **Overall judgment for `1B.4`:** **partial support on paper, weak evidence of good-faith implementation**. I found no 2024 evidence of a new signed treaty, inspection access, verified drawdown, or other concrete arms-control deliverable.

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Xi personally:
- signed or ratified a new arms-control / disarmament agreement,
- accepted inspections or verification measures,
- announced a verifiable warhead reduction,
- or took a concrete de-alerting step beyond declaratory policy.

So the record is **rhetorically supportive, operationally thin**.
